text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- National Assembly and Senate reach agreement on final draft introducing pension funds in France. A final vote is to take place on February 25, and the first pension funds put in place in autumn.
-- Skepticism rises in Europe over ability of Italy and other southern countries to meet Maastricht treaty criteria in time for monetary union.

-- Havas and Generale des Eaux hold board meetings today, expected to approve a planned increase of Generale des Eaux's stake in Havas through a transfer of its Canal Plus shares and acquisition of part of Alcatel stake in Havas.
-- Paris bourse hits new record high.
-- 14 million private-sector workers will be able to build complementary pensions through pension funds.
-- Executive committee of Thomson-CSF calls for a public sale offer for its privatisation, followed by search for European partnerships .
-- Microsoft chairman Bill Gates in Paris meets president Jacques Chirac and inaugurates exhibit of his Leonardo da Vinci Codex manuscript at the Senate.
-- U.S. ambassador to France Pamela Harriman dies in Paris.
